Habitat envelopes for the species worth hunting on this coast.
These come from published depth/habitat/temperature ranges and general
Mediterranean literature, NOT from Novigrad. They are a prior, not a
measurement. Adjust them as your dive log tells you otherwise — that is
the whole point of logging the species column.
depth_m       absolute range the species occupies
depth_best_m  where you actually expect to meet it (plateau of the fit)
relief_affinity  0-1, how tightly it holds to raised structure
slope_affinity   0-1, how much it works edges and drop-offs
temp_c / temp_best_c  water temperature tolerance and optimum
months        months it is realistically present and huntable here
viz_pref      clear  = you need clean water to get near it
any    = visibility barely changes your odds
murky  = stirred or coloured water works in your favour
wary          0-1, how much the fish punishes a noisy or visible approach
temp_c is compared against ESTIMATED TEMPERATURE AT THE SPECIES' DEPTH, not sea surface temperature - see the thermocline block in config.json.

species.note: Observed repeatedly at 4-10 m off Novigrad in Aug 2026, so the textbook 15-30 m band does not describe this shelf. Still needs clear water and a still approach.
Lives in holes, caves and under overhangs — the highest relief affinity in this list. Protected or restricted in parts of the Adriatic; CHECK THE CURRENT RULES before targeting it.
Rubble and rock edges, in holes. Barely cares about visibility and does not spook, so it salvages otherwise poor days. Best in the cooler months.
Seagrass and sand, strongly seasonal — the spring inshore spawning run is the window. Scores where rock-loving species do not.
